title: Ke ao kūlohelohe a me nā kau
description: Ten short stories about the natural world and the seasons in Hawaiʻi and beyond: gardens, waterfalls, reefs, forests, snow, coconuts, the Makahiki season and the land of Kalaupapa.

lessons.title: Ka māla ma uka
lessons.summary: In March, Leimakani's grandmother Kahiwa invites her up to Makawao; they plant young plants in the garden, set bamboo stakes beside them, and rest in the cool evening wind.
lessons.text:
Noho ʻo Leimakani me kona makuahine ma Kahului, akā noho kona tūtū wahine, ʻo Kahiwa, ma Makawao ma uka. I kēlā me kēia Malaki, kanu ʻo Tūtū i nā meakanu hou ma ka māla ma hope o kona hale.

I kēia Malaki, ua kono ʻo Tūtū iā Leimakani e piʻi mai i uka. "Ua kono mai koʻu tūtū iaʻu," wahi a Leimakani i kona makuahine. "He aha kāna hana?" i nīnau ai kona makuahine. "E kanu ana ʻo ia i nā meakanu," wahi āna.

Ma ka māla, ua hōʻike ʻo Tūtū i kekahi mau meakanu ʻōpio i loko o nā ipu. "He aha kēia mau meakanu?" wahi a Leimakani. "He mau meakanu kiʻekiʻe kēia," wahi a Tūtū. "Pono kāua e kanu i kekahi ʻohe ma ka ʻaoʻao o kēlā me kēia meakanu, i mea e kū pololei ai ia."

Ua ʻoki ʻo Tūtū i kekahi mau ʻohe lōʻihi, a ua hoʻokomo ʻo Leimakani i kēlā me kēia ʻohe i loko o ka lepo. Ua hana lāua ma ka māla a hiki i ke ahiahi.

I ke ahiahi, ua noho lāua ma waho o ka hale. Ua pā mai ka makani mai ka mauna mai, a ua hōʻoluʻolu ia iā lāua. "Hōʻoluʻolu ka makani o ke ahiahi ma uka nei," wahi a Tūtū. "Pēlā nō koʻu manaʻo," wahi a Leimakani. "ʻEha koʻu mau lima, akā ua hōʻoluʻolu ka makani iaʻu. ʻOi aku ka maikaʻi o ke ahiahi ma uka ma mua o ke ahiahi ma Kahului."

Ma mua o kona hoʻi ʻana, ua ʻōlelo ʻo Tūtū, "Ua kōkua nui ʻoe iaʻu. E kono hou ana au iā ʻoe i ke kauwela." "E hoʻi mai ana au," wahi a Leimakani. "Makemake au e ʻike i nā meakanu nui ma ka ʻaoʻao o nā ʻohe."

Nā nīnau:
Noho ka tūtū o Leimakani i hea?
Noho ʻo ia ma Makawao ma uka.
Na wai i kono iā Leimakani e piʻi i uka?
Na kona tūtū i kono iā ia.
He aha kā lāua i kanu ai ma ka ʻaoʻao o nā meakanu?
Ua kanu lāua i nā ʻohe ma ka ʻaoʻao o nā meakanu.
Pehea ka makani o ke ahiahi ma uka?
Hōʻoluʻolu ka makani o ke ahiahi ma uka.

lessons.title: Ka wailele ma Hanalei
lessons.summary: On a bright summer morning, Kaniela, his sister Kuʻualoha and their friends cross a bridge and race to a waterfall above Hanalei; Kaniela dares to jump into the clear pool, and they relax on the warm rocks.
lessons.text:
Ua pau ke kula, a ua hiki mai ke kauwela. I kekahi kakahiaka mālamalama, ua hele ʻo Kaniela me kona kaikuahine, ʻo Kuʻualoha, a me ko lāua mau hoa i kekahi wailele ma uka o Hanalei.

Ma ke ala, ua hele lākou ma luna o kekahi alahaka lāʻau ma luna o ke kahawai. Ma hope o ke alahaka, ua ʻōlelo ʻo Kuʻualoha, "E heihei kākou a hiki i ka wailele!" Ua holo ʻo Kaniela mā. Ua lanakila ʻo Kuʻualoha i ka heihei, a ua haʻaheo ʻo ia. "ʻO wau ka mea wikiwiki loa!" wahi āna.

Nani ka wailele. Hāʻule ka wai mai kekahi pali kiʻekiʻe i loko o kekahi loko wai. Akaaka loa ka wai, a mālamalama ia i ka lā.

Ua piʻi kekahi hoa ma luna o kekahi pōhaku nui, a ua lele ʻo ia i loko o ka wai. "Ua ʻaʻa ʻo ia!" wahi a Kuʻualoha. "E Kaniela, e ʻaʻa ana ʻoe?" Ua makaʻu iki ʻo Kaniela. Ua nānā ʻo ia i ka wai akaaka. Hohonu ka wai, a ʻaʻohe pōhaku ma lalo. A laila, ua ʻaʻa ʻo ia, a ua lele ʻo ia i loko o ka wai. Ua hauʻoli loa ʻo ia, a ua haʻaheo kona kaikuahine iā ia.

Ma hope, ua hoʻonanea ʻo Kaniela mā ma luna o nā pōhaku mehana. Ua ʻai lākou i nā maiʻa, a ua nānā lākou i ka wailele. Ua piha ko lākou naʻau i ka ʻoliʻoli. "He ʻoliʻoli ka hoʻonanea ʻana ma ʻaneʻi," wahi a Kuʻualoha.

I ke ahiahi, ua hoʻi lākou ma ke alahaka. "He lā hauʻoli loa kēia," wahi a Kaniela. "E hoʻi hou mai kākou ma mua o ka pau ʻana o ke kauwela."

Nā nīnau:
Ua hele ʻo Kaniela mā i hea?
Ua hele lākou i kekahi wailele ma uka o Hanalei.
ʻO wai ka mea i lanakila i ka heihei?
Ua lanakila ʻo Kuʻualoha i ka heihei.
Pehea ka wai ma lalo o ka wailele?
Akaaka loa ka wai.
Ua ʻaʻa ʻo Kaniela e lele i loko o ka wai?
ʻAe, ua ʻaʻa ʻo ia, a ua lele ʻo ia.
He aha kā lākou i hana ai ma hope?
Ua hoʻonanea lākou ma luna o nā pōhaku mehana.

lessons.title: Ka puhi ma ke kūʻono
lessons.summary: Mikala and his father swim in Hanauma Bay; they learn the bay's rules, see fish of many colours and a black fish with white dots, and find an eel hiding among the rocks that only looks angry.
lessons.text:
He kūʻono nani ʻo Hanauma ma ke kapakai hikina hema o Oʻahu. I kekahi kakahiaka, ua hele ʻo Mikala, he ʻumi ona makahiki, me kona makuakāne i ke kūʻono.

Ma mua o ka iho ʻana i ke kapakai, ua nānā nā malihini a pau i kekahi wikiō no nā lula o ke kūʻono. ʻO kēia nā lula: "Mai hānai i nā iʻa. Mai lawe i nā pōhaku. Mai luku i nā mea ola o ke kai." Ua nīnau ʻo Mikala, "No ke aha kēia mau lula?" Ua pane kona makuakāne, "Inā luku nā malihini i nā mea ola, e nalowale ana nā iʻa o ke kūʻono."

Ua komo lāua i ke kai me nā aniani. Ua ʻike ʻo Mikala i nā iʻa o nā waihoʻoluʻu like ʻole: melemele, ʻulaʻula a ʻōmaʻomaʻo. "Nani nā waihoʻoluʻu!" i manaʻo ai ʻo ia. He mau kiko keʻokeʻo ma luna o kekahi iʻa ʻeleʻele. Ua helu ʻo Mikala i nā kiko: he ʻumi kiko.

A laila, ua kuhikuhi kona makuakāne i kekahi lua ma waena o nā pōhaku. Aia he puhi i loko o ka lua! Ua hūnā ka puhi i kona kino i loko o ka lua, a ua ʻike ʻia kona poʻo wale nō. Ua wehe ka puhi i kona waha, a ua manaʻo ʻo Mikala ua huhū ka puhi.

Ma ke kapakai, ua nīnau ʻo Mikala, "Ua huhū ka puhi iā kāua?" Ua ʻakaʻaka kona makuakāne. "ʻAʻole i huhū ka puhi. Wehe ʻo ia i kona waha i mea e hanu ai. Hūnā ʻo ia i ke ao, a ʻimi ʻo ia i ka ʻai i ka pō."

Ma ka hale, ua kaha kiʻi ʻo Mikala i nā iʻa o nā waihoʻoluʻu a pau a me ka puhi, a ua kākau ʻo ia i nā lula ma lalo o ke kiʻi.

Nā nīnau:
Aia ʻo Hanauma i hea?
Aia ʻo ia ma ke kapakai hikina hema o Oʻahu.
He aha kekahi lula o ke kūʻono?
Mai hānai i nā iʻa.
ʻEhia kiko keʻokeʻo ma luna o ka iʻa ʻeleʻele?
He ʻumi kiko.
Ma hea i hūnā ai ka puhi?
Ua hūnā ka puhi i loko o kekahi lua ma waena o nā pōhaku.
Ua huhū ka puhi?
ʻAʻole, wehe ʻo ia i kona waha i mea e hanu ai.

lessons.title: Ka lei maile a me ka palai
lessons.summary: Before a hula performance, the dancer Kaumakaiwa goes into the upland forest with her teacher Kalaniʻākea; they chant before entering, gather maile and fern, and after a comedian warms up the large audience they dance a love song.
lessons.text:
He ʻōlapa ʻo Kaumakaiwa ma kekahi hālau hula ma Waimea. ʻO Kalaniʻākea kona kumu hula. I ka mahina ʻo ʻApelila, e hulahula ana nā ʻōlapa o ka hālau ma kekahi hōʻike nui, a pono lākou e hana i nā lei no ka hōʻike.

I kekahi kakahiaka, ua hele ʻo Kaumakaiwa me kona kumu i ka ululāʻau ma uka. Ma mua o ke komo ʻana i ka ululāʻau, ua kū lāua, a ua oli lāua. "Oli kākou ma mua o ke komo ʻana, no ka mea, he mea laʻa ka ʻāina," wahi a Kalaniʻākea.

Ma loko o ka ululāʻau, ua ʻohi lāua i ka maile a me ka palai. He lau liʻiliʻi ʻōmaʻomaʻo ko ka maile, a he ʻala maikaʻi kona. He lau lōʻihi ko ka palai. Ua waiho lāua i ka hapanui ma ka lāʻau, i mea e ulu hou ai ka maile.

Ma ka hālau, ua hana nā ʻōlapa i nā lei maile a me nā lei palai. ʻO ka hula a lākou e hulahula ai, he hula no kekahi ipo. Ua ʻōlelo ka mele, ua like ka ipo me ka maile o ka ululāʻau. ʻO ia ka hula punahele a Kaumakaiwa. "Punahele kēia hula iaʻu, no ka mea, ua aʻo koʻu tūtū i kēia hula iaʻu," wahi āna.

I ka lā o ka hōʻike, nui loa ka anaina. Ma mua o ka hula, ua haʻi kekahi mea hoʻokaʻakaʻa i kekahi mau moʻolelo hoʻokaʻakaʻa, a ua ʻakaʻaka nui ka anaina. Ua oli ke kumu, a ua hulahula nā ʻōlapa me nā lei maile a me nā lei palai.

Ma hope o ka hōʻike, ua ʻōlelo ʻo Kalaniʻākea i nā ʻōlapa, "He pāheona ka hula. ʻO ka oli, ka mele, nā lei a me ka hulahula ʻana, he pāheona ia mau mea a pau. Ua haʻaheo au i ka hālau."

Nā nīnau:
ʻO wai ke kumu hula o Kaumakaiwa?
ʻO Kalaniʻākea kona kumu hula.
He aha kā lāua i hana ai ma mua o ke komo ʻana i ka ululāʻau?
Ua oli lāua.
He aha nā mea a lāua i ʻohi ai?
Ua ʻohi lāua i ka maile a me ka palai.
He hula no wai ka hula punahele a Kaumakaiwa?
He hula no kekahi ipo.
Pehea ka nui o ka anaina?
Nui loa ka anaina.

lessons.title: Ke kau hāʻule lau ma Seattle
lessons.summary: Ekela from Kauaʻi studies in Seattle; in autumn the leaves turn copper, she buys warm clothes, and on the eleventh of November white snow falls, she throws snowballs and learns about steel snow chains; in history class she hears that the city is named after a native chief who signed an 1855 treaty.
lessons.text:
No Kauaʻi mai ʻo Ekela. He ʻāina kopikala ʻo Hawaiʻi: mehana ka ʻāina i ke kauwela a me ka hoʻoilo. I kēia makahiki, ke aʻo nei ʻo Ekela ma kekahi kulanui ma Seattle. ʻAʻole ʻo Seattle he ʻāina kopikala.

Ma kekahi papa mōʻaukala, ua aʻo ʻo Ekela, ua kapa ʻia ke kūlanakauhale no kekahi aliʻi ʻōiwi. I ka makahiki 1855, ua kau kēlā aliʻi i kona inoa ma kekahi kuʻikahi me ʻAmelika. Ma ia kuʻikahi, ua lilo ka hapanui o ka ʻāina o nā ʻōiwi i ʻAmelika.

I ke kau hāʻule lau, ua loli nā lau o nā lāʻau. Ua lilo kekahi mau lau i ka ʻulaʻula, a ua lilo kekahi i ka melemele. Ua lilo nā lau o kekahi lāʻau nui i ka waihoʻoluʻu keleawe. Ua loli mua nā lau ma nā wēlau o nā lālā.

He mau ʻaʻahu kauwela wale nō ko Ekela, no laila ua kūʻai ʻo ia i nā ʻaʻahu mehana.

I ka lā ʻumikūmākahi o Nowemapa, ua ala ʻo Ekela, a ua nānā ʻo ia ma ka puka aniani. Kea ka ʻāina a pau! Ua hāʻule ka hau i ka pō. Ua uhi ʻia nā kaʻa, nā hale a me nā wēlau o nā lālā i ka hau kea.

Ua komo ʻo ia i kona mau ʻaʻahu mehana, a ua holo ʻo ia i waho me kona mau hoa. Ua hana lākou i nā pōpō hau, a ua hoʻolei lākou i nā pōpō i kekahi i kekahi. Ua hoʻolei ʻo Ekela i kekahi pōpō hau i kona hoa, a ua ʻakaʻaka lāua.

Ma hope, ua ʻike ʻo Ekela i kekahi kanaka e hoʻopaʻa ana i nā kaulahao kila ma kona kaʻa. Ua hana ʻia nā kaulahao me ke kila ikaika. "No ke aha nā kaulahao?" i nīnau ai ʻo ia. "E holo ana au i nā mauna," wahi a ke kanaka. "Inā ʻaʻohe kaulahao, ʻaʻole e paʻa ke kaʻa ma ka hau."

Nā nīnau:
Ua lilo nā lau o ka lāʻau nui i ka waihoʻoluʻu hea?
Ua lilo lākou i ka waihoʻoluʻu keleawe.
I ka lā hea i hāʻule ai ka hau?
I ka lā ʻumikūmākahi o Nowemapa.
No ke aha i hoʻopaʻa ai ke kanaka i nā kaulahao ma kona kaʻa?
I mea e paʻa ai kona kaʻa ma ka hau o nā mauna.

lessons.title: Ke kai mālie i ka wā o ka ahulau
lessons.summary: In 2020 the corona epidemic closes Lopaka's Waikīkī hotel and his wife Kekilia's restaurant; his brother lends them the rent, they set aside their trip and cook rice at home, Lopaka walks in the grounds of an old fort, and on social media they see turtles return to the empty beaches.
lessons.text:
Hana ʻo Lopaka ma kekahi hōkele nui ma Waikīkī, a hana kāna wahine, ʻo Kekilia, ma kekahi haleʻaina ma kahi kokoke. Noho lāua ma kekahi hale i hoʻolimalima ʻia ma Kaimukī, a uku lāua i ka hoʻolimalima i kēlā me kēia mahina.

I ka makahiki 2020, ua laha ka ahulau kolona ma ka honua a pau. Ua pani ʻia ka hōkele o Lopaka, a ua pani ʻia ka haleʻaina o Kekilia pū kekahi. Ua ʻōlelo ka nūhou, ua emi ka helu o nā malihini ma Hawaiʻi ma kahi o 90 pākēneka.

ʻAʻohe hana a ʻaʻohe kālā. Ua manaʻo ʻo Lopaka, ʻaʻole hiki iā lāua ke uku i ka hoʻolimalima. Ua kelepona ʻo ia i kona kaikuaʻana ma Kapolei, a ua hōʻaiʻē ke kaikuaʻana i ke kālā no ʻekolu mahina o ka hoʻolimalima. "Ua hōʻaiʻē au i kēia kālā iā ʻolua. E hoʻihoʻi mai ʻolua ke hoʻi ʻolua i ka hana," wahi āna.

Ua kāpae lāua i kā lāua huakaʻi i Las Vegas, a ua kāpae lāua i nā mea a pau i pono ʻole. Ua kuke lāua i ka laiki ma ka hale i kēlā me kēia lā.

I kēlā me kēia kakahiaka, ua hele wāwae ʻo Lopaka ma ka ʻāina o kekahi pāpū kahiko ma Waikīkī. ʻAʻohe kānaka ma ka pāpū, a mālie loa ka ʻāina.

Ma ka pūnaewele pilikanaka, ua ʻike lāua i nā kiʻi o nā kahakai nele o Waikīkī. Ua hoʻi mai nā honu i ke one, a ua akaaka ke kai. Ua kākau kekahi kanaka ma ka pūnaewele pilikanaka, "Ke hoʻomaha nei ka ʻāina."

Ma hope o ʻehiku mahina o ka ahulau kolona, ua wehe hou ʻia ka hōkele a me ka haleʻaina. Ua hoʻi ʻo Lopaka a me Kekilia i ka hana, a ua hoʻihoʻi lāua i ke kālā i ke kaikuaʻana.

Nā nīnau:
Ua emi ka helu o nā malihini ma kahi o ʻehia pākēneka?
Ma kahi o 90 pākēneka.
Na wai i hōʻaiʻē i ke kālā iā lāua?
Na ke kaikuaʻana o Lopaka.
He aha kā lāua i kuke ai ma ka hale?
Ua kuke lāua i ka laiki.
He aha kā lāua i ʻike ai ma ka pūnaewele pilikanaka?
Ua ʻike lāua i nā kiʻi o nā kahakai nele.

lessons.title: Ka Makahiki ma Molokaʻi
lessons.summary: On Molokaʻi, Kaʻanohi and his father watch for the Pleiades that open the Makahiki season; at the festival in Kaunakakai the god's image is raised near a temple, the children shoot arrows at a wooden rat, a European visitor tries to pay for a lei in euros, and Kaʻanohi's crew wins the canoe race.
lessons.text:
I kekahi ahiahi o Nowemapa, ua piʻi ʻo Kaʻanohi me kona makuakāne i kekahi puʻu ma Molokaʻi e kilo i nā hōkū. "Inā ʻike ʻia ʻo Makaliʻi ma ka hikina i ke ahiahi, ua hoʻomaka ke kau Makahiki." A ua ʻike lāua iā Makaliʻi.

Ua haʻi ka makuakāne i ka moʻolelo o ka Makahiki. I ka wā kahiko, ua kaʻapuni ke akua loa i ka mokupuni. Ua hāʻawi nā kānaka i ka ʻai a me nā makana.

I ka Pōʻaono aʻe, ua hele ʻo Kaʻanohi mā i ka hoʻolauleʻa Makahiki ma Kaunakakai. Ma ke kakahiaka, ua hoʻokiʻekiʻe nā kānaka i ke akua loa ma kahi kokoke i kekahi heiau kahiko. He heiau ia no ke akua o ka Makahiki. I ka hoʻokiʻekiʻe ʻia ʻana o ke akua loa, ua oli nā kānaka a pau ma mua o ka heiau.

A laila, ua hoʻomaka nā pāʻani. I ka wā kahiko, ua pana nā aliʻi i nā ʻiole me ka pana a me nā pua. I kēia lā, ʻaʻole pana nā keiki i nā ʻiole ola; pana lākou i kekahi kiʻi ʻiole i hana ʻia me ka lāʻau. Ua pana ʻo Kaʻanohi i ʻekolu pua, a ua kū kāna pua hope loa i ke kiʻi ʻiole.

Ma ka hoʻolauleʻa, ua makemake kekahi malihini mai ʻEulopa e kūʻai i kekahi lei. Ua hāʻawi ʻo ia i 5 ʻeulo i ka wahine kūʻai lei, akā ʻaʻole i lawe ka wahine i nā ʻeulo; ua lawe ʻo ia i ke kālā ʻAmelika wale nō.

I ke ahiahi, ua heihei nā waʻa ma ke kai. Ua hoe ʻo Kaʻanohi me kona mau hoa ma kekahi waʻa liʻiliʻi. Ua hoe ikaika lākou, a ua lanakila lākou. Ua kapa ka makuakāne iā lākou he mau meʻe o ka lā. Ua hāpai ʻo Kaʻanohi i kāna hoe ma luna o kona poʻo.

Nā nīnau:
No ke aha i kilo ai ʻo Kaʻanohi a me kona makuakāne i nā hōkū?
I mea e ʻike ai lāua iā Makaliʻi.
Ua kaʻapuni ke akua loa i hea?
Ua kaʻapuni ʻo ia i ka mokupuni.
Ma hea i hoʻokiʻekiʻe ʻia ai ke akua loa?
Ma kahi kokoke i kekahi heiau kahiko.
ʻO wai nā meʻe o ka lā?
ʻO Kaʻanohi mā nā meʻe o ka lā.

lessons.title: Ke kaula niu
lessons.summary: In Lāʻie, Analu's generous grandfather Kepa teaches him to make cord from coconut husk: they cut, eat and pound the coconut, twist the fibre in equal bunches, and Analu learns not to twist with his thumb alone.
lessons.text:
Noho ʻo Analu ma Lāʻie, kokoke i ka hale o kona tūtū kāne, ʻo Kepa. He kanaka lokomaikaʻi ʻo Kepa. Hāʻawi ʻo ia i nā niu o kona ʻāina i nā kānaka a pau.

I kekahi lā, ua nīnau ʻo Analu, "E Tūtū, hiki iā ʻoe ke aʻo mai iaʻu i ka hana ʻana i ke kaula mai ka niu?" "ʻAe," wahi a Kepa. "E hoʻolako ana au iā ʻoe i nā mea a pau." Ua hoʻolako ʻo ia iā Analu i kekahi pahi, kekahi pōhaku, a me nā niu maloʻo.

Ua ʻoki ʻo Kepa i ka ʻili o kekahi niu me ka pahi. A laila, ua wāwahi ʻo ia i ka niu, a ua ʻai lāua i ka ʻiʻo keʻokeʻo o loko. "ʻOno ka niu!" wahi a Analu.

Ua waiho mua ʻo Kepa i kekahi mau ʻili niu i loko o ke kai. Ua kuʻi lāua i nā ʻili me ka pōhaku. Ua kuʻi a kuʻi lāua, a ua loaʻa nā ʻāpana lōʻihi liʻiliʻi o ka ʻili. ʻO ia ka pulu.

Ma hope, ua hilo ʻo Kepa i ka pulu ma luna o kona wāwae. "E hana penei," wahi āna. "E lawe i ʻelua ʻāpana pulu. E kaulike nā ʻāpana ʻelua. Inā ʻaʻole kaulike lāua, ʻaʻole e ikaika ke kaula. A laila, e hilo iā lāua me kou lima."

Ua hilo ʻo Analu i ka pulu me kona kōnui wale nō, a ua ʻeha kona kōnui. "Mai hilo me ke kōnui wale nō," wahi a Kepa. "E hana penei, me ka lima a pau." Ua hana ʻo Analu penei, a ua maikaʻi.

I ke ahiahi, ua loaʻa iā Analu kekahi kaula pōkole. "Mahalo, e Tūtū, no kou lokomaikaʻi," wahi āna. Ua hāʻawi ʻo Kepa i kekahi niu hou iā ia. "E lawe i kēia niu ʻono i kou makuahine."

Nā nīnau:
He aha nā mea a Kepa i hoʻolako ai iā Analu?
He pahi, he pōhaku, a me nā niu maloʻo.
No ke aha e kaulike ai nā ʻāpana pulu ʻelua?
Inā ʻaʻole kaulike lāua, ʻaʻole e ikaika ke kaula.
No ke aha i ʻeha ai ke kōnui o Analu?
No ka mea, ua hilo ʻo ia i ka pulu me kona kōnui wale nō.

lessons.title: Ka hōʻike no nā nalala
lessons.summary: Elikapeka chooses dinosaurs as the topic of her school report; she reads books and a website, writes down her sources, learns about huge bones, long necks, small brains and how bones turn to stone, and lists the dinosaurs in alphabetical order.
lessons.text:
Aʻo ʻo Elikapeka ma kekahi kula kaiapuni ma Kāneʻohe. I kekahi lā, ua ʻōlelo kona kumu, e kākau ana kēlā me kēia haumāna i kekahi hōʻike no ke ao kūlohelohe, a pono lākou e koho i kekahi kumumanaʻo. Ua koho ʻo Elikapeka i nā nalala i kumumanaʻo nona.

Ua hele ʻo Elikapeka i ka hale waihona puke. Ua heluhelu ʻo ia i ʻelua puke no nā nalala, a ua nānā ʻo ia i kekahi pūnaewele. Ua ʻōlelo ke kumu, ʻo nā puke a me nā pūnaewele i heluhelu ʻia, ʻo ia nā kūmole. No laila, ua kākau ʻo Elikapeka i ka inoa o kēlā me kēia kūmole.

Ua aʻo ʻo ia i nā mea he nui. He nunui kekahi mau nalala, ʻoi aku ka nui ma mua o ka hale. Ua loaʻa nā iwi o nā nalala nunui i loko o ka pōhaku. He lōʻihi loa ka ʻāʻī o kekahi mau nalala, a ʻai lākou i nā lau ma luna o nā lāʻau kiʻekiʻe. Akā, liʻiliʻi ka lolo o ia mau nalala.

Ma hope o ka make ʻana o kekahi nalala, ua uhi ʻia kona mau iwi e ka lepo. Ua komo nā kemika o ka wai i loko o nā iwi, a ua lilo nā iwi i pōhaku. ʻAʻohe iwi nalala ma Hawaiʻi, no ka mea, he mau mokupuni ʻōpio ko Hawaiʻi.

Ma ka hopena o kāna hōʻike, ua kākau ʻo ia i kekahi hōʻuluʻulu. Ma ka hōʻuluʻulu, ua kākau ʻo ia i nā manaʻo nui wale nō: nunui nā nalala, lōʻihi ka ʻāʻī o kekahi, liʻiliʻi ka lolo, a ua lilo nā iwi i pōhaku. Ua kākau pū ʻo ia i nā inoa o ʻumi nalala ma ke ʻano o ka pīʻāpā. "Maikaʻi ka hoʻohana ʻana i ka pīʻāpā," wahi a ke kumu.

Nā nīnau:
He aha ke kumumanaʻo o ka hōʻike a Elikapeka?
ʻO nā nalala ke kumumanaʻo o kāna hōʻike.
He aha kāna mau kūmole?
ʻO nā puke a me ka pūnaewele āna i heluhelu ai.
Pehea ka lolo o nā nalala me ka ʻāʻī lōʻihi?
Liʻiliʻi ka lolo o ia mau nalala.
Pehea i lilo ai nā iwi i pōhaku?
Ua komo nā kemika o ka wai i loko o nā iwi.

lessons.title: Ka ʻāina malu ʻo Kalaupapa
lessons.summary: Kekaula from Kaunakakai walks down the cliff trail to Kalaupapa with the guide Kauluwehi, hears that a small shield volcano made the peninsula, how people with leprosy were sent there and insulted, how they kept hope with church music and a piano, how their civil rights returned in 1969, and meets an old woman who lived there fifty years.
lessons.text:
Noho ʻo Kekaula ma Kaunakakai, ma Molokaʻi, akā ʻaʻole ʻo ia i hele i Kalaupapa ma mua. I kekahi kakahiaka, iho akula ʻo ia ma ke ala pali me kekahi alakaʻi, ʻo Kauluwehi.

Ma lalo, haʻi akula ʻo Kauluwehi i ka moʻolelo o Kalaupapa. Ua hana ʻia ʻo Kalaupapa e kekahi lua pele kuahene liʻiliʻi. Ua kahe ka pele mai ka lua pele kuahene, a ua lilo ia i ʻāina pālahalaha ma lalo o nā pali. I ka makahiki 1866, ua laha ka maʻi lēpela ma Hawaiʻi. Ua hoʻouna ke aupuni i nā kānaka me ka maʻi lēpela i Kalaupapa, no ka mea, ua makaʻu ka poʻe i ka maʻi. Ua hōʻino kekahi poʻe i ka poʻe lēpela, a ua kapa lākou iā lākou i nā inoa ʻino.

Akā, ua noho ka poʻe ma Kalaupapa me ka manaʻolana. Ua kūkulu lākou i nā hale pule, a ua hele mai ʻo Kamiano, he kahuna pule, e kōkua iā lākou. Aia kekahi piano ma kekahi hale pule. Ua hoʻokani kekahi wahine i ka piano, a ua hīmeni nā kānaka a pau.

I ka makahiki 1969, ua pau ke kānāwai kahiko, a ua hoʻihoʻi ʻia nā kuleana kīwila o ka poʻe lēpela. Akā, ua noho kekahi poʻe ma Kalaupapa a hiki i ko lākou make ʻana, no ka mea, ʻo ia ko lākou ʻāina.

Hele akula lāua i kekahi hale liʻiliʻi. Ua noho kekahi kupuna wahine ma laila no kanalima makahiki. Ua ʻōlelo ʻo ia, ua hōʻino ʻia ʻo ia i kona wā ʻōpio, akā ua lilo ʻo Kalaupapa i ʻāina malu nona. "Malu kēia ʻāina," wahi āna. "Kanalima makahiki koʻu noho ʻana ma ʻaneʻi, a ua loaʻa iaʻu ka manaʻolana ma ʻaneʻi."

I ke ahiahi, piʻi akula ʻo Kekaula ma ke ala pali.

Nā nīnau:
No ke aha i hoʻouna ai ke aupuni i nā kānaka i Kalaupapa?
No ka mea, ua makaʻu ka poʻe i ka maʻi lēpela.
Na wai i hoʻokani i ka piano ma ka hale pule?
Na kekahi wahine.
I ka makahiki hea i hoʻihoʻi ʻia ai nā kuleana kīwila?
I ka makahiki 1969.
Ua noho ke kupuna wahine ma Kalaupapa no ʻehia makahiki?
No kanalima makahiki.
